keepPolicy: a file under scripts/ or python/ that built runtime code (apps/*/lib, apps/*/dist, packages/*/*/lib, vendor/*/lib, plugins/*/lib) names by path, because deletion could break a runtime path no source check would catch `scripts/phase0/retainer.py` IS A SECOND DECLARED KEEP, added 2026-09-21: `scripts/composition/serialize-admissions.py` resolves the retainer hook RELATIVE TO ITSELF, so inside a release that file is the one a settle runs — and `scripts/**` strips it. MEASURED: without the keep the shipped retainer answers `RETAINER_UNREACHED` with `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'retainer'` while every checkout-driven arm stays green, because the checkout always has the file. The materializer copies it AND the keep preserves it, and both are required: the copy puts it in the tree, the keep stops the strip deleting it.
LICENSE, README.md, SAFETY.md and THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md at the release root

apps/cli/lib, apps/web/dist, every packages/*/*/lib with its package.json, every vendor/*/lib with its package.json, and any file a package.json lists in files or names as a concrete (non-wildcard) exports target
plugins/aukora-foundation (src, assets, lib, package.json, tsdown.config.ts): the authored AUKORA plugin, which is the reason this release exists
node_modules, pnpm-lock.yaml, package.json, pnpm-workspace.yaml and the built native addon under native/
packages/preset/agent-presets/presets, the runtime preset catalog, which no pattern above selects

scripts/aura/** and scripts/composition/** are DECLARED KEEPS, listed in strip.keep: they are the Aura lane's adapter and the composition receipt producer, verifier and serializer, which an operator runs as commands rather than bytes a built plugin names. The runtime-reference scan cannot reach them for that reason, so without a declared keep the strip deletes them and the release stops carrying the producer and verifiers while every other check stays green. They are kept so the release is self-contained for the receipt path: producer, verifier and serializer travel with the bytes they describe.

scripts/phase0/phase0log.py is a DECLARED KEEP because `scripts/**` is a strip pattern and the adapter imports it by bare name after putting scripts/phase0 on sys.path, so the strip would delete a hard dependency of scripts/aura/adapter.py while every remaining check stayed green. The RECEIPT CLOSURE is wider than the kept directories and is carried by the materializer, not by a keep: scripts/composition, scripts/aura and scripts/phase0/phase0log.py need keeps because scripts/** selects them, while vendor/append-only and vendor/receipt need only to be copied because no strip pattern selects vendor/**. Measured: a keep for a path no pattern selects is refused (strip-keep-matched-nothing), which is how this distinction was forced.

scripts/phase0/memory_head.py IS A DECLARED KEEP, added 2026-09-22: `scripts/aura/settlement.py` (SHIPPED — `scripts/aura/**` is itself a declared keep) puts scripts/phase0 on sys.path and imports `memory_head` by bare name from its settle path (`retain_memory_head`, called by `inscribe`), so inside a release this file is the one a settle runs — and `scripts/**` is a strip pattern that would delete it. The capability is memory-ledger retention: a head of Kira's memory ledger is kept OUTSIDE its state dir, so a dropped newest memory is visible instead of silently absent. That import sits on the settle path, so nothing may raise: a release missing this module does not crash and does not stay silent — it degrades to the NAMED status `MEMORY_HEAD_UNAVAILABLE` over `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'memory_head'`, which is the same shape as the retainer's own measured failure (`RETAINER_UNREACHED`) and equally invisible from the checkout, where the file is always present and every checkout-driven arm stays green. The materializer copies it AND the keep preserves it, and both are required: the copy puts it in the tree (the release tree is a clone of the built source plus named overlays, so nothing under scripts/ travels unless it is copied), the keep stops the strip deleting it. `scripts/phase0/memory-head`, the CLI entry point beside it, is deliberately NOT carried and so is not kept: the imported module is not the command, and a keep for a file the copy never placed would be refused as strip-keep-matched-nothing.

scripts/organism-accept.sh is a DECLARED KEEP alongside scripts/aura/**, scripts/composition/** and scripts/phase0/phase0log.py, and it is the one keep that is also COPIED by scripts/materialize-aukora-release.py, because the release tree is a clone of the built source plus named overlays rather than of this repository, so a keep can only preserve a file the copy already put there. It must travel because a release that cannot run its own acceptance command cannot be verified from its own bytes: the seven organism-level steps would otherwise be measurable only from the checkout that produced it, which is the reading organism-accept exists to end.

scripts/kira/** is a DECLARED KEEP alongside the paths above, and like scripts/organism-accept.sh it is also COPIED by scripts/materialize-aukora-release.py for the same structural reason: the release tree is a clone of the built source plus named overlays, so a keep can only preserve a file the copy already put there. It carries the Experience Court, scripts/kira/experience-court.py, the command listed as row 8 of plugins/aukora-kira/GRADUATION.md, which adjudicates whether a candidate record's provenance may be adopted as memory of an event. Its closure is already carried rather than widened here: the court imports `jcs` from scripts/composition, which travels for the receipt path's own reason, and it needs no plugin. It must travel because a release that cannot run its own court cannot adjudicate its own memory: the verdicts would otherwise be measurable only from the checkout that produced the release, while the release itself ships the lane whose records that court gates. CARRYING IS NOT MOUNTING AND GRANTS NO AUTHORITY: this keep carries a command an operator runs on candidate bytes; it mounts no plugin, provisions no key, adds no composition row, admits no record, and leaves production settlement unavailable as the lane's own note above records. `scripts/**` is a strip pattern the runtime-reference scan cannot reach, because no built runtime names the court by path, so without a declared keep the strip deletes it while every remaining check stays green.

scripts/lib/** and scripts/aukora/desktop-cutover.mjs ARE DECLARED KEEPS, added 2026-09-27: carried code imports them by relative path (scripts/kira/recall-probe.mjs, plugins/aukora-owner-daemon/bin/owner-daemon.mjs and plugins/aukora-subscription-hands/lib/run.mjs import scripts/lib; scripts/aura/release-boot-smoke.mjs imports desktop-cutover.mjs), and `scripts/**` deleted them. MEASURED in a scratch release: all 15 files of scripts/lib were in the strip manifest's deleted list although the materializer copied them. The materializer now refuses a release whose relative imports do not all resolve inside it (release-import-closure-open).

scanExclude.note: the installed dependency store and the generated records at the release root are copied unchanged and are never scanned or counted; Finder droppings are not release content. The skip is anchored at the root on purpose, so a node_modules inside a stripped directory leaves with that directory instead of surviving as a husk

uncoveredInputs: installed dependency bytes under node_modules: bound only by the pinned pnpm-lock.yaml digest, not by this record
native and python build products outside apps/*/lib, apps/*/dist, packages/**/lib and vendor/*/lib

files a release keeps outside the covered roots, measured on a stripped release: apps/*/tests (215 files under apps/web, 131 under apps/cli, 40 under apps/desktop), apps/desktop (46 files of editor, not loaded by the web profile), native/ (85 files, including the built addon), per-package metadata beside each lib (package.json, README, cordis.patch.yml) and the runtime preset catalog under packages/preset/agent-presets
runtime files loaded from outside the covered roots (private state, plugin drop-ins, generated profiles)
network, clock, environment variables and telemetry inputs that can change behavior without changing bytes
limits: The record is producer attestation from the run that wrote it. This checker detects missing or changed covered artifacts, deleted or rewritten records, coverage-declaration drift and dependency-pin drift.

A producer that rewrites both a covered artifact and the whole record consistently is NOT detectable for host-only files until a release digest is pinned in committed source; the upstream client record anchors only the client face.
Cross-machine byte reproducibility is not claimed; the record describes one build on one toolchain.

The strip manifest is producer evidence, but the consumer does not trust it: it re-derives the selection from the declared strip patterns, so a path the rules select fails the check even when the manifest omits or agrees with it. The manifest's after-state totals are re-measured on every full-tree check, which is what keeps the number in the manifest honest.

plugins/aukora-composition-gate/src and its package.json are covered because the gate is a LAUNCH-TIME dependency: the launcher installs its policy as a node bootstrap, so altering it changes what the running process enforces. It is covered by the same record as the foundation plugin for the same reason — not because it is decorative.

plugins/aukora-composition-gate/policy.json is covered by an EXACT host pattern because it is where the GOVERNED ID LIST lives: the launcher writes its `governed` array into gate-config.json, so editing this one file changes WHICH plugin ids the running process refuses at import without changing a single line of code. It was previously declared only in genesisPatterns, and that is the asymmetry this line closes: genesisPatterns describe the CHECKOUT, hostPatterns describe the RELEASE, and only hostPatterns reach buildRecord/verifyArtifacts for a release tree. Measured on a materialized release: a record rewritten to drop policy.json from its entries used to verify CLEAN, because the covered-path set was derived from hostPatterns and the file was not in it. PATTERNS MATTER HERE AND SO DOES THE EXACT FORM: `plugins/*/policy.json` would cover it too, but it would also silently select a policy.json added by any future plugin, so the boundary of what this pattern governs would drift with the plugin directory listing instead of with the gate.

patterns are resolved against the tree they describe: genesisPatterns against the Genesis worktree and hostPatterns against a materialized release. A release-generated file such as demo-governed.patch.yml must be declared in hostPatterns — declaring it in genesisPatterns matches nothing there and silently covers nothing, because only an all-empty set fails.

plugins/aukora-kira/lib and its package.json are covered because they are the SHIPPED plugin bytes: the lane's load-bearing code is what a release would mount, so altering it must fail the record rather than pass unnoticed. The lane's tests, its test store and its measurement artifacts are NOT covered and are not part of any composition. CORRECTED: this note previously implied the release does not carry the plugin. It does now — the materializer copies the lane sources, and coverage follows from the release's own plugin host patterns. The lane is still NOT mounted, its test store is not carried, and production settlement remains unavailable (KIRA_SETTLEMENT.available = false).

plugins/aukora-aumlok/lib and its package.json are covered because they are the SHIPPED plugin bytes: altering the adapter or its control service must fail the record rather than pass unnoticed. The lane's tests and review material are NOT covered, following the precedent of the composition gate and the foundation plugin. CORRECTED: an earlier version of this note said materializing a release does not copy these bytes. That became false when the materializer was changed to carry the lane sources, and a note describing the old behaviour is worse than no note. The materializer now copies plugins/aukora-kira and plugins/aukora-aumlok (lib and package.json) into the release, where the release's own plugins/*/lib/**/* and plugins/*/package.json host patterns cover them. CARRYING IS NOT MOUNTING: neither plugin is in any composition row, and an unprovisioned mount still refuses by name.

The Aumlok owner signer is covered for two distinct reasons, and only one of them is byte integrity. scripts/aumlok/signer.mjs is the CLI a person actually runs to approve an operation, so a change to it changes the thing that claims to carry an owner decision. Its suite, tests/aukora-aumlok-signer.test.mjs, was covered too until the test forest was archived on 2026-09-27 (ARCHIVE.md); it is no longer in the tree, so it is no longer a pattern. The signer is written as an exact path, and their presence IN THE WRITTEN RECORD was measured rather than assumed — a pattern that matches nothing is a silent no-op here, and only an all-empty Genesis set is refused. The signer's channel modules (owner-signer.mjs, signer-channel.mjs) are shipped plugin bytes covered by the aumlok plugin lib pattern, which the adapter-CI round adds; on a tree carrying the signer code without that round these exact paths are the only signer coverage, which is why they are not deferred to it.

The Aura adapter and the composition layer are carried in the release as DECLARED KEEPS and covered by both genesisPatterns (the source they are copied from) and hostPatterns (the copies in the release). Carrying them makes the receipt path self-contained and makes those bytes tamper-evident; it does not mount them, does not give them authority, and does not mean the running application reads them from the release. Measured: the lane's own suites invoke the producer and the adapter from the CHECKOUT, not from the release.

Generated debris is EXCLUDED from coverage by path: **/target/**, **/__pycache__/**, **/*.pyc and **/*.pyo. This matters because vendor/append-only is a genesisPattern and genesisPatterns resolve against the checkout, where CI builds the Rust replica into replicas/rust-verifier/target/ (gitignored) and where importing a script writes a cache. Without the exclusions the record would hash cargo artifacts and bytecode — a record that depends on what a build left behind instead of on the reviewed bytes, and one that changes when a developer runs a test locally. The materializer applies the same exclusions when it copies, so the release and the record agree about what is debris.

scripts/aumlok/diagnose.mjs is covered as an exact path. It is the lane's own inventory of what is PACKAGED, MOUNTED and PROVISIONED — the three claims that get blurred in conversation — so altering it must fail the record rather than pass unnoticed. Five suites were exact-path genesisPatterns until the test forest was archived on 2026-09-27 (ARCHIVE.md): tests/aukora-foundation.bundle.test.mjs, tests/aukora-foundation.install.test.mjs, tests/aukora-aumlok-signer.test.mjs, tests/kira-memory-owner.test.mjs and tests/kira-approval.test.mjs. They are no longer in the tree, so they are no longer patterns, and the record covers no test suite.

`aukora-nostr/**` is a HOST pattern and `plugins/aukora-nostr/**` its genesis twin, added 2026-09-22 so the tree the Messages host half resolves at runtime travels with the release and is tamper-evident. The two spellings differ because the TREES differ, and that difference is measured rather than stylistic: the face loads `<its own lib>/../../../aukora-nostr/lib/contact.mjs`, and the materializer keeps a release's faces FLATTENED at `plugins/aukora-face-messages/lib/index.js` — one directory shallower than the checkout's `plugins/aukora-face/messages/lib/index.js` — so the release-side copy sits at the release ROOT while the source it is copied from sits under `plugins/`. `plugins/*/lib/**/*` DOES NOT COVER IT: that pattern resolves against the release, where the copy is `aukora-nostr/lib/**`, so leaving it to that pattern would keep the bytes the release actually loads outside the record. Measured by importing a release's own face bytes and calling its exported `resolveContactModuleSpecifier()`: the root copy resolves to `<release>/aukora-nostr/lib/contact.mjs`; the same bytes under `plugins/aukora-nostr/` are not a candidate at all and the call refuses with `messages:nostr-tree-absent`. The materializer copies the WHOLE tree, so these two patterns are the complete boundary of it, and NO `strip.keep` entry accompanies them: no strip pattern selects `aukora-nostr/**`, and a keep for a path no pattern selects is refused as `strip-keep-matched-nothing`.
